sections.heading: M1: System, Model, And Simulation
sections.summary: A system is a collection of interacting or interdependent elements working toward an end. A model represents that system physically, mathematically, or logically, while a simulation imitates its operation over time or space. Modeling and simulation is a problem-based discipline for repeatedly testing hypotheses and supporting decisions. Its four precepts are modeling, simulation, visualization, and analysis.

key_terms.definition: The subject being investigated, including relevant people, hardware, software, facilities, policies, and documents.
A representation of a system, entity, phenomenon, or process.
Using or executing a model to investigate behavior.
A proposed physical system that does not yet exist.

properties.name: Study Route
properties.statement: Choose the actual system or a model; choose a physical or mathematical model; for a mathematical model choose analytical evaluation or simulation.

properties.name: Modeler Priorities
properties.statement: Quantify behavior, support system design/control/use, and measure performance.

properties.name: Falling-Object Equations
properties.statement: With initial velocity v0=100 ft/s, initial height s0=1000 ft, and a=-32 ft/s^2: h(t)=0.5*a*t^2+v0*t+s0=-16*t^2+100*t+1000; v(t)=100-32*t.

properties.name: Page 13 C Code, Not MATLAB
properties.statement: The slide uses float h, v = 100.0, s = 1000.0; int t; for (t = 0, h = s; h >= 0.0; t++) { h = (-16.0 * t * t) + (v * t) + s; printf("Height at time %d = %f\n", t, h); }. Its comment reverses height and velocity; its loop tests the preceding height before updating, so it can print a negative height.

steps: Ours: MATLAB translation of the page 11 equation and page 13 C calculation; fixed times avoid the C loop termination issue.

Page 13 height values do not follow its own equation: at t=1 and t=2 the correct heights are 1084 and 1136 ft.
Notional does not mean impossible to model.

sections.heading: M1: Boundaries, Components, And Modeling Principles
sections.summary: The boundary decides which activities belong to the system and which come from its environment. Entities are objects, attributes are their properties, and activities change the system; the state records the relevant condition at one time. Establish the structure first, then supply attribute values and activity relationships as data. Model only what the study needs, using accurate information and an appropriate amount of aggregation.

key_terms.definition: An object of interest.
A property of an entity.
A process causing system changes.
Relevant entities, attributes, and activities at a specified instant.
What lies outside the chosen system boundary.

properties.name: Deriving A Model
properties.statement: Structure: set boundary and identify entities, attributes, activities. Data: provide attribute values and define activity relationships.

properties.name: Boundary-Dependent Example
properties.statement: Page 19 lists supermarket purchasing/checkout as endogenous and customer arrivals as exogenous. Its parking example lists supermarket customer arrival as endogenous and car arrival as exogenous; interpret this only after stating the boundary.

properties.name: Reasons To Model
properties.statement: Model when the actual system is inaccessible, dangerous, unacceptable to engage, or not yet in existence.

worked_examples.problem: Identify entity, attribute, and activity for a bank.
steps: Choose a customer as the object of interest.
Record account number and balance as properties.
Treat a deposit as a state-changing process.
worked_examples.answer: Entity: customer. Attributes: account number and balance. Activity: deposit.

common_mistakes: An event is not inherently endogenous or exogenous; its classification depends on the declared boundary.
Sampled-data does not mean the underlying dynamics are discrete.
Aggregation groups entities; it does not guarantee greater accuracy.

sections.heading: M1: Study Process, Solutions, And Supporting Disciplines
sections.summary: Analytical methods use mathematics to obtain exact or general results under a model's assumptions when the model is tractable. Simulation evaluates configured scenarios numerically when interactions or constraints make analysis difficult. Both require a sound model, and simulation is not automatically cheap, quick, or random. A useful study repeatedly defines the problem, builds and checks the model, experiments, and interprets results.

key_terms.definition: Mathematical evaluation using algebra, calculus, or probability.
Checking that implementation correctly represents its specified model.
Checking model suitability for the real purpose.
Turning generated data into interpretable performance information.

properties.name: Seven-Step Simulation Process
properties.statement: 1 Define problem; 2 introduce important variables; 3 construct simulation model; 4 specify values to test; 5 conduct simulation; 6 examine results; 7 select best course of action. Revisit model or test values when results require it.

properties.name: Ten Model-Building Steps
properties.statement: 1 Define achievable goal; 2 assemble complete skill mix; 3 involve end user; 4 choose tools; 5 choose detail; 6 collect input data early; 7 document continuously; 8 plan verification; 9 plan validation; 10 plan statistical output analysis.

properties.name: History As Presented
properties.statement: 1940s Monte Carlo for neutron scattering, associated with John von Neumann, Stanislaw Ulam, Edward Teller, Herman Kahn; 1960s SIMSCRIPT and special-purpose languages; 1970s mathematical foundations; 1980s PCs, GUIs, object orientation; 1990s web simulation, animation, optimization, MCMC.

common_mistakes: Do not copy page 33 as a guarantee that simulation takes only minutes or little money.
Verification is not a substitute for validation.
Random variation limits stochastic predictions, not every possible simulation.

sections.heading: M1: Classifications, Paradigms, And Model Detail
sections.summary: Classifications answer different questions, so a model can be dynamic, stochastic, and discrete at the same time. Monte Carlo emphasizes random sampling, continuous simulation follows continuously evolving states, and discrete-event simulation changes state at event times. Fidelity measures realism, resolution measures detail, and scale measures the size of the represented scenario. Choose the paradigm and detail needed for the question rather than assuming more detail is always better.

key_terms.definition: Closeness to reality for the intended behavior.
Granularity or degree of detail.
Size or level of the overall scenario.
Combining more than one modeling paradigm.

properties.name: Continuous Example
properties.statement: Page 43 displays V(t)=V_DD*(1-exp(-t/(R*C_L))). This is an ideal RC charging relation; do not assume it is a full nonlinear transistor model.

properties.name: DES Example
properties.statement: The emergency-department picture traces arrival, triage, waiting, treatment, disposition, discharge or inpatient-bed waiting/admission, with a leave-without-being-seen branch.

properties.name: Other Model Types
properties.statement: The slides also name Markov chains, finite-state automata, particle systems, queueing models, bond graphs, and Petri nets.

properties.name: Other Simulation Types
properties.statement: Hybrid combines approaches; real-time coordinates modeled and wall-clock time; web-based describes delivery/access rather than a requirement for randomness.

common_mistakes: Randomness and treatment of time are separate classification axes.
High resolution does not ensure high fidelity.
The page 47 games are illustrative slide comparisons, not universal rankings of realism.

memory_aids.label: Ours, Not The Slides
memory_aids.text: FRS: Fidelity, Resolution, Scale. Remember their meanings as realism, detail, and scenario size.

sections.heading: M1: Participation, Applications, And Domains
sections.summary: Participation categories distinguish who acts and whether the operated systems are real or simulated. Applications describe why the simulation is built, while domains describe the subject area. Constructive simulations still receive real human inputs even though their represented actors and systems are simulated. The same domain can support training, analysis, experimentation, engineering, or acquisition.

key_terms.definition: Real people operate real systems.
Real people operate simulated systems.
Real people supply inputs carried out by simulated people operating simulated systems.
The subject area of the M&S process.

properties.name: Slide Examples
properties.statement: Live: CyberSurgeons classroom activity; virtual: A320 flight simulator; constructive: ModSAF combat model for doctrine and engagement rules.

properties.name: Engineering Tools
properties.statement: The slides identify finite element tools, MATLAB for continuous modeling, and ARENA for discrete-event systems.

properties.name: Application Examples
properties.statement: Manufacturing, weapons/logistics, communication and computer requirements, transportation, service organizations, business-process redesign, inventory control, production planning, and finance/economics.

properties.name: Named Software And Scope
properties.statement: AnyLogic demonstrates GIS supply chains/logistics; GeoFS demonstrates global flight simulation; Morild Interaktiv demonstrates maritime VR training. Page 71 names GNS3, Cisco Packet Tracer, PuTTY, SecureCRT, Microsoft Visio, PRTG Network Monitor, Wireshark, EVE-NG, NS3, and SNMP Agent Simulator, but terminal clients, diagramming, monitoring, and packet-analysis tools are not all simulators.

common_mistakes: Do not classify constructive as having no real human involvement.
Domain is not the same as application purpose.
A product appearing on the network-tools slide is not proof it performs simulation.

sections.heading: M1: MATLAB Workspace, Variables, And Classes
sections.summary: MATLAB means Matrix Laboratory and provides computation, visualization, and programming in a matrix-based language. The Command Window accepts commands, the workspace shows variables, the Current Folder shows files, and Command History records earlier commands. Numeric values default to double, while casts deliberately select other numeric, character, or logical classes. MATLAB needs no imports for the built-in commands taught here.

key_terms.definition: Variables available in the active execution context.
The data type of an array.
Conversion using a class function such as int32(num).
A one-element, 1-by-1 array.

properties.name: Help And Session Commands
properties.statement: Exact command names: demo; help; help help; lookfor; doc; quit; exit. demo/doc open help interfaces, help explains functions, lookfor searches help, and quit/exit end MATLAB. These are reference syntax, not replay checks.

properties.name: Page 80 Command-History Expressions
properties.statement: The desktop example includes res = 9 - 2; num = res; x = 1:4;. Command History recalls commands, while Workspace shows the variables currently retained.

properties.name: Names And Assignment
properties.statement: Start with a letter; continue with letters, digits, underscores; names are case-sensitive and cannot be keywords. namelengthmax gives the supported maximum. Avoid shadowing built-ins. Slide expressions: mynum = 6; 6 + 3; res = 9 - 2;. An unassigned result uses ans, and a trailing semicolon suppresses automatic display.

properties.name: Workspace Commands
properties.statement: who lists names; whos includes size/bytes/class. Exact slide cleanup syntax: clear; clear variablename; clear variablename1 variablename2. Slide trace: mynum = 3; mynum + 5; clear mynum. These workspace-dependent commands are documented, not used for output checks.

properties.name: Classes And Casting
properties.statement: Numeric classes: single, double; signed int8, int16, int32, int64; unsigned uint8, uint16, uint32, uint64. Text shown with single quotes is char; logical stores true/false. Slide code: num = 6 + 3; numi = int32(num);. class(num) identifies a class; single(num), double(num), char(num), logical(num) illustrate corresponding conversions.

properties.name: Ranges
properties.statement: Use intmin('int8') and intmax('int8'); the signed range is -128 through 127. Unsigned uint8 includes zero and reaches 255. The slides recommend int32 when an integer type is needed.

properties.name: Format And Scientific Notation
properties.statement: Exact forms: format short; format long; format loose; format compact. These affect display, not stored precision. Slide expressions: 2 * sin(1.4); 2 * 10^4; 2e4. The last two represent the same number.

properties.name: MATLAB Background
properties.statement: Originally exposed LINPACK and EISPACK matrix software; supports matrix manipulation, algorithms, plotting, multiple programming paradigms, Simulink/Model-Based Design, and interaction with C, C++, Java, Python, and .NET. The page 74 C bit-field image is not MATLAB syntax or an import requirement.

sections.heading: M1: MATLAB Operators, Functions, And Special Values
sections.summary: Operators distinguish assignment, comparison, logical decisions, and numerical calculation. Parentheses make precedence explicit and help prevent accidental changes in meaning. Many mathematical functions act elementwise, but reduction functions follow separate dimension rules. Character encoding examples use ASCII values, although MATLAB character handling is not limited to ASCII.

key_terms.definition: The = operator stores a value.
Relational operators return logical results.
&& and || evaluate scalar conditions and can skip an unnecessary right-hand operand.
log(x) is the logarithm to base e, not the value e.

properties.name: Arithmetic And Delimiters
properties.statement: Exact taught syntax: +, -, *, /, \, ^, .*, ./, .\, .^, :, (), [], ., ..., comma, semicolon, %, =, apostrophe ('), and dot-apostrophe (.'). % begins a comment outside text; within fprintf format text it introduces conversion specifications. ... continues a statement onto the next line.

properties.name: Relational And Logical Syntax
properties.statement: <, <=, >, >=, ==, ~=; &&, ||, ~, xor. Slide expressions: 3 < 5; 2 > 9; 2 < 4 || 'a' == 'c'; xor(3 < 5, 'a' > 'c'). Use parentheses, then powers, unary operations, multiplication/division, addition/subtraction, relations, AND, OR as the practical slide precedence order.

properties.name: Rounding And Remainders
properties.statement: fix(x) truncates toward zero; floor(x) rounds down; ceil(x) rounds up; round(x) rounds to nearest. mod(x,n) and rem(x,n) are remainder functions with different negative-argument conventions. Exact slide syntax includes rem(13, 5) and nthroot(64, 3).

properties.name: Functions And Units
properties.statement: sign(x) is -1, 0, or 1 for negative, zero, positive real values; sqrt(x), nthroot(x,n), log(x), log2(x), log10(x), exp(x), sin(x), sind(x), abs(x). sin uses radians and sind uses degrees.

properties.name: Additional Page 92 Functions
properties.statement: Exact names: asin, sinh, asinh, asind, rand, rng, clock, randn, randi. Syntax completions (ours, not slide examples): asin(0.5); sinh(1); asinh(1); asind(0.5); rng(1); rand(2,3); randn(2,3); randi(10,2,3); clock;. These demonstrate inverse/hyperbolic functions, random-state control, random arrays, and current date/time; no fixed random or clock output is claimed.

properties.name: Constants And Characters
properties.statement: pi is the circle constant; i and j are imaginary units unless shadowed; inf/Inf denotes infinity; NaN denotes an undefined numeric result. Exact character examples: double('a'); char(97); double('abcd'); char('abcd' + 1);. Apostrophe conjugates complex values as it transposes; dot-apostrophe only transposes.

== tests equality; = assigns.
% is not a modulo operator.
log(x) does not equal e.
Do not use short-circuit && and || as substitutes for elementwise logical array operations.

sections.heading: M1: Vectors, Matrices, And Indexing
sections.summary: A matrix has rows and columns, while a vector has only one row or one column. Construct rows using spaces or commas and separate rows using semicolons. MATLAB indexing starts at one and gives row before column for matrix subscripts. size, length, and numel answer different questions and should not be interchanged.

key_terms.definition: A 1-by-n array.
An n-by-1 array.
An element index, starting at 1.
Joining compatible arrays along a dimension.

properties.name: Exact Page 93 Shape Examples
properties.statement: Scalar [5]; column [3;7;4]; row [5,88,3,11]; matrix [9 6 3;5 7 2]. Their shapes are 1-by-1, 3-by-1, 1-by-4, and 2-by-3 respectively.

properties.name: Creation Syntax
properties.statement: Exact slide examples: v = [1 2 3 4]; v = [1,2,3,4]; vec = 1:5; nv = 1:2:9; c = [1;2;3;4]; r = 1:3; c = r'; mat = [4 3 1;2 5 6]; m = [1 2 3;4 5 6;7 8 9];. All rows in an ordinary matrix must have equal lengths.

properties.name: Concatenation Syntax
properties.statement: Exact page 96 setup and forms: r1 = [1 2 3 4]; r2 = [5 6 7 8]; r = [r1,r2]; rMat = [r1;r2]; c1 = [1;2;3;4]; c2 = [5;6;7;8]; c = [c1;c2]; cMat = [c1,c2];. Horizontal joins need matching row counts; vertical joins need matching column counts.

properties.name: Vector Subscripts
properties.statement: Slide setup: newvec = [1 3 5 7 9 3 6 9 12 15]; newvec(5); b = newvec(4:6); newvec([1 10 5]); b(2) = 11;. A list of indices can select nonadjacent entries in the requested order.

properties.name: Matrix Subscripts
properties.statement: Exact slide setup: mat = [2:4;3:5]; mat(2,3); mat(1:2,2:3); mat(1,2) = 11;. In mat(row,column), the first argument always selects rows.

properties.name: Dimension Syntax
properties.statement: length(vec), size(vec), [r,c] = size(mat), length(mat), numel(mat). Additional slide setups: vec = -2:1; vec = 9:-2:1; mat = [3:2:7;9 33 11];.

properties.name: Empty And Deletion Syntax
properties.statement: Slide code: evec = []; length(evec); evec = [evec 4]; evec = [evec 11]; vec = 4:8; vec(3) = [];. Remaining vector elements are reindexed. The illustrated mat(1,2) = [] is invalid two-subscript deletion of one matrix cell, since it leaves a nonrectangular hole; deleting a full row/column is different.

length(matrix) is its largest dimension, not total element count.
The colon operator creates a row; transpose it for a column.
A rectangular matrix cannot lose one cell through two-subscript deletion.

sections.heading: M1: Reshaping, Rearrangement, And Reductions
sections.summary: Rearrangement changes shape or positions without changing the values being represented, while replication makes copies. reshape preserves MATLAB's columnwise linear order and must preserve the element count. Mathematical functions such as sin and sign usually act elementwise, but sum, prod, min, and max reduce along a dimension. For ordinary matrices with multiple rows, these reductions work down columns by default; specifying dimension two works across rows.

key_terms.definition: Reinterpret the same elements with new dimensions.
Combine several entries into fewer values.
Running totals/products that preserve vector length.
Tiling copies into a larger array.

properties.name: Rearrangement Syntax
properties.statement: Exact slide syntax: mat = randi(100,3,4); reshape(mat,2,6); fliplr(mat); flipud(mat); rot90(mat); intmat = randi(100,2); repmat(intmat,3,2);. randi output is random; reuse a saved matrix instead of expecting the same values on each call.

properties.name: Elementwise Function Syntax
properties.statement: Slide examples: vec = -2:1; sinvec = sin(vec); mat = [0 4 -3;-1 0 2]; sign(mat);. This size-preserving rule does not cover every MATLAB function.

properties.name: Vector Reduction Syntax
properties.statement: Exact examples: vec1 = 1:5; vec2 = [3 5 8 2]; min(vec1); sum(vec1); max(vec2); prod(vec2); cumsum(vec1); cumsum(vec2); cumprod(vec1);.

properties.name: Column Reduction Syntax
properties.statement: Slide setup: mat = randi([1 20],3,5); max(mat); sum(mat);. min(mat) and prod(mat) follow the same default reduction convention for this shape.

properties.name: Rows And Output Orientation
properties.statement: Exact slide examples: max(mat'); sum(mat'); max(mat,[],2); sum(mat,2);. Also use min(mat,[],2) and prod(mat,2). Transposing first yields row-oriented row summaries; dimension 2 returns a column of summaries.

properties.name: Default-Dimension Qualification
properties.statement: The general MATLAB rule is first nonsingleton dimension. Thus a 1-by-c row vector reduces to one scalar rather than being treated as c independent one-element columns.

repmat(A,m,n) means m-by-n copies, not a final m-by-n element array.

sections.heading: M1: Array Operations And Matrix Algebra
sections.summary: Scalar multiplication or division scales each array element. Array multiplication, division, and power use a dot so that corresponding elements are combined. Matrix multiplication instead sums row-by-column products and needs matching inner dimensions. Determinants are defined for square matrices, and transpose exchanges row and column roles.

key_terms.definition: Operate on corresponding compatible array entries.
A row-by-column sum of products.
A scalar property of a square matrix.
Compatible singleton dimensions expand for array operations in modern MATLAB.

properties.name: Dotted Operator Syntax
properties.statement: v = [3 7 2 1]; v.^2; v1 = 2:5; v2 = [33 11 5 1]; v1.*v2;. Division syntax is A./B or A.\B. + and - are already elementwise and do not need a dot.

properties.name: Shape Compatibility Correction
properties.statement: Page 113 teaches equal-size arrays. Equal sizes are sufficient, but modern MATLAB also supports compatible singleton dimensions: (1:3)' + (1:2) forms a 3-by-2 result.

properties.name: Matrix Product Rule
properties.statement: If A is m-by-n and B is n-by-p, A*B is m-by-p. C(i,j)=sum over k of A(i,k)*B(k,j). Ordinary / and \ are matrix divisions, not corresponding-entry array division.

The product keeps outer dimensions only after the inner dimensions match.
Do not add dots to + or -.
For complex matrices, apostrophe also conjugates.

self_check.question: How do system, model, and simulation differ?
self_check.answer: The system is the subject, the model represents it, and simulation operates that model.

self_check.question: Does observing a continuous system once per second make it a discrete system?
self_check.answer: No. This is sampled-data observation of underlying continuous dynamics.

self_check.question: How do fidelity, resolution, and scale differ?
self_check.answer: Realism, detail, and represented scenario size respectively.

self_check.question: What does sum return for a general 2-by-3 matrix, and what about sum(A,2)?
self_check.answer: sum(A) is 1-by-3 column totals; sum(A,2) is 2-by-1 row totals.

self_check.question: What distinguishes A*B from A.*B?
self_check.answer: Matrix multiplication sums row-column products and matches inner dimensions; elementwise multiplication combines corresponding compatible entries.

self_check.question: Which baseline slide corrections are easy exam traps?
self_check.answer: sign(0)=0; log is base e, not equal to e; unsigned integers include zero; page 13 heights are 1084 and 1136 at t=1,2; not every function preserves shape.

cram_sheet.remember: System -> representation/model -> execute/simulate -> analyze decisions; MSVA precepts.
Boundary first; entity object, attribute property, activity change; data fills values and relationships.
Static/dynamic, deterministic/stochastic, continuous/discrete are independent axes.
Verify implementation, validate purpose, analyze stochastic outputs; simulation is not automatically cheap or random.
Fidelity realism; resolution detail; scale size. Live real/real, virtual real/simulated, constructive simulated/simulated.
No imports needed. Default double; valid case-sensitive names; format affects display only; % comments, == compares, = assigns.
One-based indexing, row then column; size shape, numel count, length largest dimension; reshape columnwise; reductions usually down columns.
.* ./ .^ are elementwise; * is matrix product; transpose changes shape; det needs square input.
